pr_body:
When the existing `--transitions` flag is set to a non-None value,
cquery will report the configuration its dependencies are configured in.
This allows for pruning away values from ruleInputs which are not
required in the current configuration.

Example output from running:
`bazel cquery --transitions=lite --output=jsonproto 'deps(...)'`:
```
[...]
        "ruleInput": ["@bazel_tools//src/conditions:host_windows", "@bazel_tools//src/tools/launcher:launcher", "@bazel_tools//tools/launcher:launcher_windows"],
        "configuredRuleInput": [{
          "label": "@bazel_tools//src/tools/launcher:launcher",
          "configurationChecksum": "01ec5513a9fc41b2a15570123817f3c2200ad9aeb21b1181d588a4b4f91d5693",
          "configurationId": 3
        }]
[...]
```

Previously on a non-Windows platform it was not possible to determine
that the two windows-specific ruleInputs are not actually required - now
we can see from the configuredRuleInput section that the
windows-specific dependencies have been pruned by selection, and we can
see that a transition has re-configured the ruleInput into the exec
configuration.

For dependencies which were not subject to transition (e.g. because
they're in a non-transition attribute), or which had no configuration
(e.g. because they're a source file), we add the label as a
ConfiguredRuleInput _without_ any configuration information. This
indicates that the dependency has not been pruned, but that the caller
should determine the correct configuration from context (probably be
determining whether it's a source file, and if so, considering it
un-configured, otherwise propagating the contextual ConfiguredTarget's
configuration).

Fixes #14610
Fixes #14617

Implementation-wise, this took roughly the following shape:
1. Extract TransitionResolver from being inline in TransitionsOutputFormatterCallback
2. Extract KnownTargetsDependencyResolver from TransitionsOutputFormatterCallback.FormatterDependencyResolver
3. Conditionally call these from ProtoOutputFormatterCallback depending
   on the --transitions flag.

issue_context.title: cquery returns rule_input targets which are missing from deps list
issue_context.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

Chasing the chain of `rule_input`s from running `cquery` on a `java_test` target, I see the following chain:

```
//java/example:ExampleTest
->@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:toolchain
->@local_config_cc//:toolchain
->@local_config_cc//:cc-compiler-armeabi-v7a
->@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes
```

In particular, here's where I see `@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes`:

```
% bazel cquery '@local_config_cc//:cc-compiler-armeabi-v7a' --output=jsonproto 2>/dev/null | jq '.results[].target.rule.ruleInput'
[
  "@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/cc/whitelists/parse_headers_and_layering_check:disabling_parse_headers_and_layering_check_allowed",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/cc/whitelists/starlark_hdrs_check:loose_header_check_allowed_in_toolchain",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:interface_library_builder",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:link_dynamic_library",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes",
  "@local_config_cc//:empty",
  "@local_config_cc//:osx_tools_armeabi-v7a",
  "@local_config_cc//:stub_armeabi-v7a"
]
[
  "@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/cc/whitelists/parse_headers_and_layering_check:disabling_parse_headers_and_layering_check_allowed",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/cc/whitelists/starlark_hdrs_check:loose_header_check_allowed_in_toolchain",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:interface_library_builder",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:link_dynamic_library",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes",
  "@local_config_cc//:empty",
  "@local_config_cc//:osx_tools_armeabi-v7a",
  "@local_config_cc//:stub_armeabi-v7a"
]
[
  "@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/cc/whitelists/parse_headers_and_layering_check:disabling_parse_headers_and_layering_check_allowed",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/cc/whitelists/starlark_hdrs_check:loose_header_check_allowed_in_toolchain",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:interface_library_builder",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:link_dynamic_library",
  "@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes",
  "@local_config_cc//:empty",
  "@local_config_cc//:osx_tools_armeabi-v7a",
  "@local_config_cc//:stub_armeabi-v7a"
]
```

And this target seems to exist:

```
% bazel cquery '@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes' 2>/dev/null                                                           
@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes (51eca89)
```

But it's not returned in `deps(//java/example:ExampleTest)` or `somepath(//java/example:ExampleTest, @bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes)`:

```
% bazel cquery 'somepath(//java/example:ExampleTest, @bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes)' 2>/dev/null

% bazel cquery 'deps(//java/example:ExampleTest)' 2>/dev/null | grep -c '@bazel_tools//tools/objc:host_xcodes'
0
```

The target _does_ show up using `query` not `cquery`, so maybe this is a duplicate of https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/14610 where the root issue is that `rule_input`s don't get configuration filtered, but target dep edges do?

Either way, it doesn't seem like there's a way to trace "Here are the files which impact this target in the current configuration", except possibly by performing a per-target `deps(target)` query - trying to batch this into a single `deps(...)` query seems to take away the ability to filter by configuration?

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

macOS

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

release 4.2.1

/cc @gregestren
comments: this is the duplicate of [1406](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/14610). See comment https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/14610#issuecomment-1025523391. On the top of my head, I do not think it's possible to achieve what you want in a single cquery because cquery runs over the result of the analysis phase instead of the loading phase. The work around doing per-target deps(target) query  you mentioned makes sense to me. @illicitonion is this a blocker for you?

> I do not think it's possible to achieve what you want in a single cquery because cquery runs over the result of the analysis phase instead of the loading phase.

This is where I'm a bit confused - https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/14610#issuecomment-1025523391 suggests that the problem here is that we're using Target messages from the loading phase, but as cquery uses the results of analysis, I'd expect the Target messages to be refined with the information we gained by doing further analysis. It feels like come analysis time we must _have_ (or at least be able to construct) a filtered down Target message, but we happen to be re-using the one from the loading phase? So the real request here is to refine the returned Target using the information we gained by doing further analysis. Does that make sense as a problem statement?

> The work around doing per-target deps(target) query you mentioned makes sense to me.

Yeah, it's a functional workaround, but as we're doing whole-repo queries, that necessitates doing many thousands of individual queries, and the overhead of a single bazel invocation to do a query on a pre-warmed graph is hundreds of milliseconds, so doing per-target queries would add hours to the query pipeline, which is definitely not a usable solution.

> @illicitonion is this a blocker for you?

Yeah, this is a pretty hard blocker - right now we're both over-estimating which targets we need to run (by following edges which don't have relevant configurations), and ignoring errors (because if things are missing from the query, we have to assume they were `select`ed out, rather than that something went wrong in the graph structure or our parsing logic).

It would be great to discuss whether there are important reasons for us to be returning the loading-phase `Target`, or whether we could refine that down to a post-configuration `Target` with more precise information. I'm happy to dig into the code and try to put together a fix, with a little mentoring...

Thanks!

What does this mean?

This was copied and pasted from `TransitionsOutputFormatterCallback`. I think what it's saying is: `processOutput` only has two checked exceptions it's allowed to throw, `IOException` and `InterruptedException`, so rather than changing the `processOutput` API (a larger change), or throwing a `RuntimeException` (generally frowned upon in Java, but 🤷 seems better than this), hide the error in an `InterruptedException`.

I tried adding the exception to the interface, but ended up with a cyclic dependency because it ended up needing the `com.google.devtools.build.lib.cmdline.BatchCallback` interface (very high-level) to depend on the analysis package (very low level).

I could use a `RuntimeException`, or introduce a new Exception type, but I assume whoever originally wrote this code decided it was not worthwhile.

[This code](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/6594e0ca76305464f7f43ee236b21699ac4d3892/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/query2/engine/OutputFormatterCallback.java#L45-L59) has an even sketchier hack, we could do something similar if we needed?
